s: Out of the persons given below, who freed the Indian press from restrictions?
x: Charles Metcalfe's Press Act of 1835 freed the Indian press; Bentinck is the tempting option.

s: In which of the following year was the freedom of press given by Lord William Bentinck?
x: The press was freed in 1835 by the Metcalfe Act (passed by Metcalfe as acting Governor-General after Bentinck's departure, so linked with the Bentinck era).

s: What did the Act V of 1843 make illegal?
x: Act V of 1843 abolished slavery (Ellenborough); Sati was banned in 1829.

s: Which Governor General had abolished slavery?
x: Slavery was abolished by Act V of 1843 under Lord Ellenborough (1842-44); Bentinck's Charter Act of 1833 only asked for it.

s: From the following Britishers, who is credited for removal or banned on newspapers?
x: Charles Metcalfe removed the restrictions on newspapers by the Press Act of 1835.

Consider the following statements related to Wellesley’s administration.

I. In the six years of Wellesley’s administration, the army accounted for 42.5 per cent of the company’s total expenditure.

x: Richard Wellesley described himself as the 'Bengal Tiger'; Clive was the 'heaven-born general'.

Which one of the following measures was not one of them?
o: Abolition of Titles and Pensions of Several Rulers

x: Dalhousie's Railway Minute (1853) pressed for rapid railway building.

s: Who of the following passed the Widow Remarriage Act ?
x:
Most books and keys: Dalhousie. Strictly: the Act (XV of 1856) was passed on 26 July 1856 under Lord Canning (Rocket Sheets list it under Canning).
NextGen and Spectrum list the Widow Remarriage Act (1856) under Dalhousie (1848-56); it was drafted in his time and became law on 26 July 1856, after Canning had taken over.

s: Public Works Department was organized in 1845-1855 by –
x: Dalhousie (1848-56) set up the Public Works Department (1854); before him public works were under the Military Board.

s: Under whose Governor-Generalship, the Railways were introduced in India?
x: Railways began in 1853 under Dalhousie (1848-56).

s: Dalhousie has been regarded as the maker of modern India because he brought about reforms and made a beginning in many fields. Which one among the following was not one of his schemes of reforms?
o: Construction of railways and introduction of telegraph and postal services.
Establishment of a public works department.
Factories Act to improve the condition of Indian labour.
x: Railways, telegraph, post and the PWD were Dalhousie's; the first Factories Act (1881) came under Ripon. Wood's Despatch (1854) makes 'educational reforms' his too.
